WHY THIS WEBSITE

Beyond simply showcasing technology,
an open laboratory where we study together is what we aim to build.

Based on decades of field experience and research, CNR Korea has studied and developed environmental and energy technologies related to water, energy, waste, resource circulation, and carbon neutrality. On this website, we present the current development status of 10 technologies as it is — openly and without embellishment.

Some technologies have reached prototype testing, some are in the final stages of development or prototype testing, and others remain concepts requiring further engineering review and demonstration. Researchers, engineers, students, companies, universities, research institutes, and anyone interested in the future of environment and energy are welcome to participate.

TECHNOLOGY 01

Multi-Stage Fluid Acceleration Power Generation System

Prototype Tested / Prototype Production

This power generation system redirects reverse flow inside a duct back into the forward-flow direction and merges it with the main flow, increasing the useful flow through the turbine. The flow-management structure is designed to reduce unnecessary vortices and impact, lower vibration and noise, and improve power-generation efficiency. It is being developed for application to wind, hydro, tidal, thermal, and steam energy.

CNR KOREA Internal Prototype Test More than 2× the power-generation efficiency of the comparison configuration · Efficiency above 50% confirmed

These figures are based on CNR Korea’s internal prototype tests and measurements. Before commercial application, reproducibility will continue to be verified through repeated testing under identical conditions and independent measurement.

How We View the Betz 59.3% Limit

This device is not an open, single wind turbine alone; it is a complete ducted system that collects and accelerates fluid and converts reverse flow back into forward flow for reuse. Therefore, CNR Korea does not treat the Betz limit of 59.3% as a directly applicable performance limit for the entire system. Performance is evaluated by measuring actual input and output energy.

What We Need to Study and Verify Together
  • Power output and actual generation efficiency under comparative conditions
  • Fluid-flow and pressure changes before and after reverse-flow → forward-flow conversion
  • Reduction of vibration · noise · vortices
  • Performance differences in wind · hydro · steam applications
  • Long-duration durability and reproducibility under independent measurement
TECHNOLOGY 02

Multi-Stage Recirculating Fluid Acceleration Propulsion System

Final Development Stage

This propulsion system automatically separates and draws in forward flow and reverse flow at the intake stage, organizes and accelerates them through internal passages, then recombines and discharges them in one direction. It is designed to minimize vortices, cavitation, vibration, and noise caused by direct reverse-flow collision, while merging recovered fluid energy into the forward propulsion stream to generate strong thrust.

Core Flow Structure Automatic separation and intake of forward/reverse flow → acceleration → mixed discharge

We are studying and verifying a structure that separates and organizes fluid flow, then recombines and discharges it in one direction to reduce vortices, cavitation, vibration, and noise while increasing thrust.

What We Need to Study and Verify Together
  • Simultaneous measurement of actual thrust · input power · flow rate
  • Effects of automatic forward/reverse-flow separation and recirculation
  • Reduction of vortices · cavitation · vibration · noise
  • Thrust increase from mixed discharge
  • Propulsion efficiency versus input power and long-term structural durability
TECHNOLOGY 03

Hybrid Electric Ship Using Onboard Wind & Hydro Power

Concept · Engineering Study

Conventional ships take in and discharge ballast water during ballast voyages to maintain draft and stability. CNR Korea’s concept uses through-hull water channels for both hydro power generation and propulsion, while operating electric main and auxiliary propulsion systems selectively according to operating conditions. The goal is an eco-friendly electric ship that minimizes ballast-water intake and discharge. Onboard wind and hydro generation support battery charging and propulsion power. Hull forms can be designed in various configurations according to vessel purpose and navigation area, including passenger ships, container ships, cargo ships, tankers, naval vessels, and ships operating in inland waters such as the Great Lakes.

Core Goal · Minimize Ballast-Water Intake & Discharge

Through-hull water channels. We are studying how hydro generation and auxiliary propulsion using through-hull water channels, together with selective operation of electric main/auxiliary propulsion, can reduce ballast operation required during ballast voyages.

GenerationOnboard wind + through-hull hydro→Battery · onboard power
PropulsionMain propulsion + auxiliary propulsion→Selective operation by voyage condition
BallastDraft control during ballast voyage→Minimize intake · discharge
EnvironmentOily/wastewater · waste · exhaust gas→Recovery · reuse · carbon management
What We Need to Study and Verify Together
  • Ship stability and feasible ballast minimization under ballast and loaded conditions
  • Hydro generation from through-hull channels and impact on hull resistance
  • Power and thrust allocation between main and auxiliary propulsion
  • Energy balance among wind/hydro generation and battery capacity
  • Demonstration and certification review under safety · classification · IMO requirements
TECHNOLOGY 04

Next-Generation Onshore & Offshore Wind Power System

Final Development Stage

Unlike conventional large wind turbines that seek stronger winds at greater heights, this concept uses ducts and intake structures to guide wind toward the turbine while locating the power-generation unit at a comparatively lower level.

Easier MaintenanceSimplified StructureReduced Noise & VibrationOnshore · Offshore · Building Applications
Next Verification Tasks
  • Long-duration generation performance in natural wind
  • Safe operation and protection under typhoon conditions
  • Structural safety at larger scale
  • Objective comparison with conventional wind turbines under identical conditions
TECHNOLOGY 05

Wastewater Treatment & Treated-Water Reuse System Using Thermal Power

Final Prototype Testing

An integrated water-treatment and energy-recovery system intended for sites that generate sewage or wastewater, including semiconductor plants, mines, pharmaceutical companies, and wastewater treatment facilities. Steam produced during wastewater treatment drives a steam turbine to generate and supply electricity. After power generation, the steam is cooled and condensed back into water, purified according to its intended use, and reused. In an era of increasing water scarcity, the key is to obtain both electricity and reusable water while treating wastewater.

GoalWastewater Treatment+Generation+Waste-Heat Recovery+Water Reuse+Carbon Management
Key Advantage Sewage/Wastewater Treatment → Steam Power Generation → Treated-Water Recovery & Reuse

Steam produced during sewage and wastewater treatment is used to generate electricity, then recovered as water after power generation and reused in a resource-circulation process.

Priority Applications & Current Key Tasks

Semiconductor plants · mines · pharmaceutical companies · industrial complexes · municipal wastewater treatment plants The system targets diverse sewage and wastewater streams from these and other facilities. CNR Korea particularly sees a strong need to shift from discharging treated municipal wastewater to reusing it. Current work includes final steam-turbine testing and verification of wastewater-specific pretreatment, energy balance, and recovered-water quality.

TECHNOLOGY 06

Seawater Desalination System Using Thermal Power

Final Prototype Testing

An integrated heat-electricity-water system that uses steam produced while heating and evaporating seawater to generate electricity through a steam turbine, then condenses the steam and recovers it as fresh water. By using the same steam energy for power production, the system aims to reduce external electricity demand and the net fossil-fuel burden of steam production, improving desalination economics.

Seawater→Preheating · Evaporation→Steam Turbine→Condensation→Purification · Reuse
Economic Structure Freshwater Production + Electricity Generation + Waste-Heat Recovery

Thermal energy used for evaporation is continuously utilized for steam power generation, and after generation the steam is recovered as fresh water. Actual fuel savings and economics will be verified through full heat-balance analysis and long-duration operation tests.

Current Key Tasks
  • Final steam-turbine testing and electricity output
  • Heat-recovery rate · overall energy efficiency · actual fuel savings
  • Freshwater output and stage-by-stage water-quality performance
  • Concentrate management and corrosion · scale control
  • Water-quality standards and long-duration verification for potable-water applications
TECHNOLOGY 07

Submersible Barge-Type Hydro & Tidal Power System

Concept · Engineering Study

A barge-type generation system fabricated on land or at a quay, moved to the installation site, filled with water and submerged, then used to generate electricity from river, tidal, or ocean currents. When necessary, it can be refloated and moved to a maintenance location.

RiversTidal AreasOcean CurrentsAround BarragesZigzag Multi-Unit Arrangement
Items to Review Together
  • Scour prevention and foundation stability
  • Floating debris · waste management
  • Submergence · refloating stability
  • Response to floods and water-level changes
  • Civil works · maintenance · economics
TECHNOLOGY 08

AI Data Center Power Supply, Cooling & Power Recovery System

Research & Development in Progress

AI data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity, while additional power is required to remove the heat generated by computing and to circulate cooling air. CNR Korea is developing a new energy-recovery approach designed to recover usable energy that would otherwise be dissipated through heat removal, cooling, and airflow processes and convert it back into useful electrical energy, with the goal of reducing the net power demand of the cooling system and the data center as a whole.

Core R&D TargetMore than 80% recovery of recoverable energy associated with cooling and air-circulation processes

Our research includes operating scenarios in which cooling represents around 40% of total electricity use. The 80% figure does not mean 80% of total data-center electricity; it is the R&D target for energy that is technically recoverable within the cooling and air-circulation process. Actual recovery efficiency and total data-center power reduction will be validated through repeated testing and full-scale demonstration.

Power Supply→AI Computing→Heat Generation→Cooling & Air Circulation→Energy Recovery→Reuse

Core Direction

Reduce wasted energy, recover what can be recovered, and minimize the net power demand of future AI data centers. The research also explores integration with next-generation wind power, hydropower, tidal power, waste-to-energy and ESS.

Current Research Direction
  • Electrical-energy recovery from recoverable energy otherwise lost during cooling and air circulation
  • Reduction of cooling load through multi-stage heat exchange and higher cooling-system efficiency
  • Integrated power supply using next-generation wind, hydro, tidal, waste-to-energy and ESS
  • Comparative verification of fan power, airflow, recovered generation and net electrical consumption before and after energy recovery
  • Validation of actual recovery efficiency and total power reduction through repeated testing and full-scale demonstration
TECHNOLOGY 09

Carbon-Neutral Resource-Circulating Future City Integrated Platform

Integrated Platform · In Development

A future-city environmental platform that connects municipal and industrial waste, wastewater, power generation, water reuse, exhaust-gas cleaning, and carbon management in a single circular system.

Waste→Combustion · Heat Recovery
Waste Heat + Wastewater→Steam · Power Generation
Post-Generation Steam→Condensation · Recovered Water
Exhaust Gas→Multi-Stage Scrubber · CO₂ Capture

Goal

Waste into energy, wastewater into reusable water, recovered resources back to the city. By integrating individual technologies, the platform aims to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower carbon emissions in a circular urban system.

TECHNOLOGY 10

Aircraft Emergency Auxiliary Propulsion & Air Brake System

Concept · Engineering Study

A next-generation aircraft concept that combines a Rotating-Blade Speed-Increasing Power Generation Device with a Multi-Stage Recirculating Fluid Speed-Increasing Propulsion Device. During flight, the propulsion device can operate as an auxiliary propulsion unit. During landing, it is deployed from its stowed compartment, rotated 180°, and switched to Air Brake Mode. The power-generation device can provide auxiliary electrical power during flight for battery charging and electric propulsion. The long-term concept also studies conversion of the main propulsion system to an electric-motor-driven system. The goals are improved safety, reduced energy consumption, and progress toward carbon neutrality.

During FlightMulti-Stage Recirculating Fluid Speed-Increasing Propulsion → Auxiliary Propulsion
Power GenerationRotating-Blade Speed-Increasing Power Generation Device → Battery Charging
During LandingDeploy from Stowed Compartment → 180° Rotation → Air Brake Mode
Essential Future Verification
  • Reliability of main propulsion · auxiliary propulsion · air-brake mode transitions
  • Aerodynamics and changes in drag · lift
  • Structural · weight · vibration · noise impacts
  • Wind-tunnel tests · ground tests · staged flight tests
  • Aviation safety standards and certification; electric-propulsion system safety

COMMERCIALIZATION & PILOT PROJECTS

Commercialization & Pilot Projects

These projects apply CNR Korea’s core technologies to practical field problems and examine pilot-scale performance and commercialization potential. They are presented as applications rather than as an 11th core technology.

APPLICATION PROJECT 01

Site-Adaptive Pumping Power Optimization and Flow Energy Recovery System for Aquaculture Farms

Pilot · Investment · Partnership

The concept selectively applies Hydro Power Generation Units 1, 2 and 3 according to site conditions such as intake flow, natural water flow, water-level difference, discharge flow and piping conditions. Recovered electricity is stored in an ESS and reused to operate the aquaculture pumping system.

Intake / Natural Flow→Hydro 1·2·3→ESS→Pump→Aquaculture Farm
Commercialization GoalMinimize the pump’s net external electricity demand

The project is intended to recover usable flow energy from natural inflow, water-level difference and discharge water, then verify the relationship between recovered generation and pump consumption through field measurement and pilot testing.

Site-Adaptive Configuration
  • Hydro Power Generation Unit 1: generation using seawater inflow created by pumping
  • Hydro Power Generation Unit 2: generation using discharge-water flow driven by aquaculture-farm water pressure rather than head alone
  • Hydro Power Generation Unit 3: generation using large water flow and velocity
  • Recovered electricity is stored in an ESS and reused for pump operation
  • At sites with sufficient external hydraulic energy, pilot tests will examine whether recovered generation can approach or exceed pump electricity consumption
  • Future plan: develop and manufacture a pumping unit optimized for this system

※ Actual power savings and generation depend on site head, flow rate, piping losses, pump efficiency and operating conditions and must be verified by field measurement.

PROVEN FIELD EXPERIENCE

Environmental Technology Born in the Field

CNR Korea’s future-technology research did not begin with ideas alone. Experience accumulated in real-world work—including ship waste handling, marine pollution response, oil-tank cleaning, waste-oil treatment, and wastewater treatment—became the foundation for technology development.

2007

Hebei Spirit Marine Pollution Response

After the accident, we carried out ship cleaning and restoration work to help vessels return to safe operation. This experience became a practical foundation for marine-pollution response, ship cleaning, and future research into marine and soil environmental restoration technologies.

“The field was the best textbook.”

FUTURE ENVIRONMENT & DISASTER RESPONSE

Large Wildfire Suppression Using Helicopters

Idea · Concept Study

This idea is not included among the 10 core technologies. It is proposed as a separate future environmental and disaster-response study aimed at reducing forest destruction, carbon emissions, casualties, and environmental damage caused by large wildfires.

The concept seeks to reduce the risks of direct human entry into major wildfire zones by linking helicopters with high-capacity ground water-supply systems for continuous delivery of large volumes of firefighting water. According to the project materials, the idea was inspired by field experience using multiple connected hoses to supply water and oil offshore where tank trucks or supply vessels could not directly approach.

Preliminary Review Tasks
  • Helicopter safety and flight stability
  • Weight and dynamic loads of hoses · piping
  • Ground water-supply system and intermediate storage tanks
  • Aviation safety · operating plan · applicable regulations
  • Model Testing → Staged Field Verification
Nothing changes without action.Idea → Calculation → Design → Testing → Verification

The technologies presented on this website are not all at the same development stage. CNR Korea does not hide those differences; we begin by accurately showing how far each technology has progressed.

I will share what I know. Where my knowledge is insufficient, I want to study together. What is wrong should be corrected through testing and verification, and what proves promising should be developed together.

FOUNDER & CEO

Seonggeun Son

CEO, CNR Korea Co., Ltd.

After graduating from the Department of Navigation at Korea Maritime & Ocean University in 1983, I worked at sea as a merchant marine officer for approximately 12 years. I later founded Seohae Petroleum and carried out field work involving ship-generated waste, waste-oil and wastewater collection, and environmental services, building experience in marine environmental work, waste-oil and wastewater treatment, and environmental restoration on land and at sea. In 2024, I founded CNR Korea, an environmental technology R&D company.

Could wasted energy be used again?

Could polluted water be made clean again?

Could we produce energy while treating waste?

Could we use the power of wind and water even a little more effectively?

That is how I have come this far—studying and testing one idea at a time. I do not believe I know everything. On the contrary, I believe there is still much to learn. I want to pass on what I know to those who come next, and study together with others where my knowledge is incomplete.

Among the environmental technologies I have learned and studied in the field for nearly 40 years,
to complete and verify even one more of them with confidence and pass it on to the next generation—
that is my dream and my goal.

If even one good technology is completed and used anywhere in the world to clean water, save energy, and reduce carbon emissions, I believe that alone would make the effort worthwhile.

A MESSAGE FOR THE NEXT GENERATION

Let us learn together · research together · test together · and build together.

Let us share the knowledge we have, study together where knowledge is lacking, test possibilities together, and verify the results accurately so that we can build better technologies for the next generation.

Let us pursue carbon neutrality and solve environmental problems one by one, so that we can pass on to our descendants an Earth even a little cleaner than the one we inherited.

Thank you.
Sincerely, Seonggeun Son
CEO · CNR Korea Co., Ltd.
